overall_notes: Slate has merit but several legs are either fairly priced with thin edges or carry material unpriced risk (blowout, platform issues, noisy markets). Solid keeps: Sengun volume, Coward boards, Towns/Podziemski strong recent form vs weak opponents. Cuts: Johnson has flawed reasoning (faster pace + worst defense = MORE assists risk, not less), Mitchell has platform verification gap, Stone/Dorofeyev face elite/well-priced defense. My knowledge cutoff is Feb 2025, so 2026 season data verifies the given statistics but team identity/role changes are what I'm assessing.

votes.reasoning: Reasoning contains a logical flaw: Chicago's fastest pace and worst defensive rating should create MORE assist opportunities, not fewer, which contradicts the under thesis. Johnson's recent 6-of-9 under 8 is real, but gaining 5.8 minutes from Newell's injury should help, not hurt an assists prop. Line at -154 (~58%) is fairly priced; no edge here.

Strong volume thesis: Sengun has 14+ FGA in 9 of 10 and 5 of 5 recent with Capela/Adams/Smart all out. Even if Houston blows out Utah (real risk at -15.5), Sengun's role is likely protected enough to reach 14 FGA. Book -130 (~55% fair) leaves room. Blowout could suppress 4Q volume but frontcourt consolidation should hold.

Solid setup: Memphis loses Edey and Post (direct board impact), New Orleans loses Missi (opposing reb threat), total 236.5 with both teams top-half pace. Coward 9-of-10 over 7 with recent 8.7 average is strong. Book -112 is nearly fair but slightly favors overs. Board play should hold.

Critical blocker: FGM market availability on PrizePicks/Underdog not verified, making entry uncertain or impossible. Beyond that, 10-straight 5+ FGM at -190 (~63% fair) is tightly priced, and Klay Thompson questionable introduces variance. Thin margin with platform risk is disqualifying.

Turnovers are notoriously noisy and high-variance; even a 10-straight streak is fragile. Wagner's 2.5 line is tight with -165 fairly pricing the 60% edge. Real blowout risk (ORL -8.5 vs 1-11 MIL) could suppress 4Q usage and lower creation attempts. TO props rarely have clean edges.

Strong matchup: Towns averaging 41 P+R in last 3, 10-game double-double streak, road average 35 P+R, faces Indiana's documented center weaknesses (52.2% FG allowed to centers, bottom-10 vs fives). Line 33.5 is beatable. NY -8.5 blowout risk is real but Towns's recent form suggests he hits even with limited 4Q.

Very thin line at 1.5 with 9-of-10 hitting 2+, yet priced at -150 (~58% fair). While the track record suggests higher hit rate, the 1.5 line margin is razor-thin and heavily same-game correlated with L6. Correlation risk plus tight margin make this a low-priority leg that doesn't justify the variance.

Excellent load concentration: Curry (oblique), Butler, Moody, and Porzingis all out means Podziemski is the primary ballhandler and volume driver. Last 2 games 32, 31 PRA with 29.4 PRA/36 without Curry is elite. 24.5 line is reasonable. SA -11.5 blowout risk is material but even limited 4Q minutes likely gets him there given recent usage.

Despite -196 being the slate's strongest-priced SOG line, Nashville is elite defensively (5th-fewest SOG allowed, 2nd-best save%). At 1.5 SOG against elite D, the market is fairly pricing or slightly undervaluing Nashville's defensive strength. Mark Stone is good but 1.5 SOG vs elite defense is appropriately hostile. No edge.

Material risk: New York is on back-to-back (played at Calgary Nov 12), and SOG output is sensitive to fatigue in the first period. Recent L10 average 3.0 SOG masks variance (3,6,3,4). FD -130 (~54%) is fairly priced, but back-to-back fatigue is likely underpriced. Thin edge with real fatigue risk.
